module_name: Apply the new brand identity across the web app
criteria: In App.tsx, palette.primary becomes main '#10875A', light '#3FB489', dark '#0B5E3F'. palette.secondary and palette.background are left exactly as they are.
In the same createTheme call, typography gains fontFamily: 'Georgia, "Times New Roman", Times, serif'. The existing h4 and h5 fontWeight entries stay.
Nothing else in App.tsx changes: no new ThemeProvider, no dark mode, no component overrides, no routing changes, no new imports other than what the theme needs.
The AppBar in Navbar.tsx keeps having NO colour prop and no background in its sx: the navbar turns emerald green purely through the theme.

Navbar.tsx gains AccountBalance to its existing @mui/icons-material import block, and the PMBButton exactly as given above. Two of its values are checked literally: the Button's child text is exactly 'PMB', and its href is exactly 'https://pmb.ro'. The icon is AccountBalance, the label is not.

PMBButton is rendered in the Toolbar AFTER the navigation Box and BEFORE the role Chip, so it sits on the right-hand side next to the role chip. It is not filtered by hasRole and is not part of getNavigationItems(), so every signed-in user sees it in both navigations.

In LoginPage.tsx every hardcoded old-blue value is replaced: '#1976d2' -> '#10875A', '#42a5f5' -> '#3FB489', '#1565c0' -> '#0B5E3F'. The gradients keep their exact structure (135deg, same stops), only the colours change. Nothing else in that file changes.
getRoleColor in Navbar.tsx is NOT changed: traveller stays '#1976d2'. Role colours encode role identity, not branding.
`npm run type-check` and `npm run lint` in RouteOptimizer.Web both pass.
